subject: Intermittent 502 pattern affecting streaming responses — status update & next steps
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Rachel Turner <rachel.turner@solstice.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Intermittent 502 pattern affecting streaming responses — initial status notice

Hi Rachel,

Quick update from Redwood: we’re seeing an intermittent pattern of 502 responses affecting in-progress streaming requests for the Solstice AI integration starting ~08:45 PDT. Our status page has been updated with a notification: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/20270420-streaming-502s

Impact (current):
- A subset (~3-7%) of streaming generation requests to the hosted API return an immediate 502 and terminate mid-stream.
- Affected endpoints: /v1/chat/stream and /v1/generate/stream for your US-west region key.
- No evidence of data loss; request logs show connection resets at the gateway layer.

What we’re doing now:
- Engaged serving runtime team to trace gateway->backend handoffs and KV cache interactions.
- Applying a temporary routing policy to route traffic to a sibling pool that has applied an updated gateway retry fix (targeted in next 20–30m).
- Monitoring for false positives and continued end-to-end verification with a small canary of your production traffic.

Immediate ask from Solstice: can you confirm whether you saw any client-side retries or duplicates? Also, if you have any jobs relying on long-lived streaming connections, we’ll coordinate a brief maintenance window to failover traffic cleanly.

I’ve attached a snapshot of the status page and our mitigation checklist. I’ll follow up with a short post-incident note once we stabilize and capture timeline + root cause.

Apologies for the disruption — we’ll keep this thread updated.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Account Lead, Strategic Customers
Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.ai
Attachments: statuspage-incident-snapshot.png (image/png); mitigation-checklist.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Rachel Turner <rachel.turner@solstice.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 09:37:14 -0700
Subject: Re: Intermittent 502 pattern affecting streaming responses — initial status notice

Thanks Karthik — appreciate the quick heads up.

We saw elevated 502s in our observability around 08:50 and have a handful of user-facing failures. We did not observe retries originating from our SDK; our logging shows the client received a 502 and surfaced an error to the user.

Two asks:
1) ETA for the sibling-pool reroute and whether that will require any changes on our side.
2) If you expect any duplicate events once retries are enabled on the gateway, we need to know so we can dedupe downstream.

We can pause any long-lived streaming experiments for the next hour if that helps with the canary.

—Rachel
Rachel Turner
Head of Integrations, Solstice AI
rachel.turner@solstice.ai

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 12:05:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Intermittent 502 pattern affecting streaming responses — next steps and post-incident actions

Marissa / Aditya / Laura — forwarding the customer reply. Short internal plan and asks below.

Timeline so far (brief):
- 08:45 PDT: traffic spike + gateway connection resets begin for a subset of long-running streaming requests.
- 09:10 PDT: status page posted and customer notified.
- 09:25 PDT: initial routing policy applied; canary traffic successfully routed to sibling pool with the gateway retry patch.
- 09:40–11:30 PDT: error rate dropped to baseline for canary; gradual ramp of full traffic completed by 11:15.

Immediate action items (owners):
- Marissa: coordinate a formal post-incident timeline and compile the request logs (gateway, LB, backend) for 08:30–12:00 PDT. Please include the sample request ids flagged by Solstice.
- Aditya: validate that the gateway retry change does not introduce duplicate delivery semantics. Confirm retry policy (idempotency) and whether we should expose a retry header for customers to dedupe. Target: 24h.
- Laura: confirm whether this incident needs an SLA credit discussion with Sales/Ops and draft a short customer-facing postmortem bullet list by EOD. Include proposed wording that avoids technical jargon but explains root cause & mitigations.

We should schedule a 30m sync with Solstice tomorrow morning to walk through the timeline and remediation steps. Rachel — can you do 09:00–09:30 PDT tomorrow? We’ll send a calendar invite once we confirm.

I’ve attached the mitigation checklist and the status snapshot for the record. Follow the incident playbook: tag this with incident-20270420 and push logs to the incident bucket.

Thanks,
Karthik
